item.title: Ambiguity/Conflict at Crossroads, 20th August
item.description:
Road Safety Report: Downhills Way / Lordship Lane Subject: Proposed amendment to lane-use arrangements to reduce side-swipe, merging and near-miss conflicts 1. Purpose of this report This report proposes a relatively simple change to the lane-use arrangement at the Downhills Way crossing of Lordship Lane. The aim is to reduce the potential for vehicles in Lane 1 and Lane 2 to converge into the same path, particularly where the road layout reduces from three lanes to two. 2. Existing arrangement At present, Lane 1 is marked for left turn and ahead, while Lanes 2 and 3 are marked for ahead. A 'No Right Turn' restriction is also in place. This arrangement means that drivers using Lane 1 for the ahead movement can find themselves having to negotiate the reduction from three lanes to two, creating a potential conflict with traffic travelling in Lane 2. 3. Safety concern There have reportedly been a number of collisions and near-misses at or around this lane reduction. The concern is that drivers may naturally follow the road markings and continue ahead from Lane 1 while vehicles in Lane 2 are also travelling ahead. As the available lanes reduce, the two streams of traffic are required to occupy fewer lanes, increasing the opportunity for sudden braking, lane changes, side-swipes or uncertainty over priority. 4. Proposed change The recommended change is to make Lane 1 compulsory LEFT only, rather than LEFT and AHEAD. Lanes 2 and 3 would remain for the ahead movement, subject to the Council's traffic-engineering assessment. The change should be made clear through appropriate advance direction signs, lane arrows and other road markings so that drivers have sufficient warning before reaching the junction. Illustrative concept The following original schematic illustrates the proposed principle. It is not a measured engineering drawing and should not be used for construction or traffic-order purposes. 5. Why the proposal may improve safety • Reduces conflicting movements: drivers in Lane 1 would no longer be invited to continue ahead into the lane-reduction area. • Provides clearer lane discipline: the ahead movement would be concentrated into Lanes 2 and 3. • Gives drivers a simpler decision: Lane 1 drivers make a left turn; drivers wishing to continue ahead position themselves in Lanes 2 or 3. • Potentially reduces last-minute lane changes: clearer advance markings could discourage drivers from attempting to move across lanes immediately before the reduction. • Improves predictability: a compulsory direction is generally easier for drivers to understand than a shared left/ahead lane where the road geometry subsequently reduces the number of lanes. 6. Recommendation to Haringey Council Haringey Council's highways and road-safety team should investigate the collision and near-miss history at this location and undertake a formal road-safety assessment. If the assessment supports the concern, the Council should consider changing Lane 1 to a compulsory left-turn lane, supported by clear advance signage and road markings. The Council could also review visibility, lane widths, stop-line positioning, signal phasing and the transition from three lanes to two as part of the assessment. 7. Conclusion The proposed alteration is intended to remove an avoidable point of uncertainty at the lane reduction. Making Lane 1 compulsory LEFT, while retaining Lanes 2 and 3 for ahead traffic, could provide a clearer and more predictable movement pattern. Given the reported collisions and near-misses, a formal review by the Council would be justified.
